title: Tense Lab
intro: Tense is about time and about how the speaker sees the action: finished or still going, a fact or a temporary thing, planned or decided now. Each unit shows the time on a line, the pattern, the traps Bangla speakers fall into, and then drills from real situations.
introBn: বাংলায় আমরা অনেক সময় একই রূপ দিয়ে কাজ চালাই, কিন্তু ইংরেজিতে সময় আর কাজের অবস্থা (শেষ হয়েছে কিনা, এখনো চলছে কিনা) দেখে tense বাছতে হয়।

units.title: Present simple vs present continuous
units.idea: Simple = facts, habits, permanent things. Continuous = happening around now, temporary, changing.
units.ideaBn: Simple মানে নিয়মিত বা স্থায়ী সত্য; continuous মানে এই মুহূর্তে বা এই কদিন সাময়িকভাবে চলছে।

timeline.label: now: I'm working from home this week

formula.name: Simple
formula.q: Do you work? Does she work?

uses.rule: Permanent situation vs temporary one.
uses.bn: স্থায়ী হলে simple, সাময়িক হলে continuous।
uses.ex: She lives in Sylhet, but she's staying with her aunt this month.

uses.rule: Stative verbs (know, believe, want, need, belong, seem, own, prefer) are not normally continuous.
uses.bn: মনের অবস্থা বা মালিকানা বোঝানো verb সাধারণত -ing নেয় না।
uses.ex: I know the answer. (not: I am knowing)

uses.rule: Some verbs change meaning: think (opinion) vs thinking (considering), have (own) vs having (doing), see (understand) vs seeing (meeting).
uses.bn: একই verb দুই অর্থে দুই রূপ নেয়।
uses.ex: I think it's expensive. / I'm thinking of buying it.

uses.rule: Always + continuous = an annoying repeated habit.
uses.ex: He's always leaving the gate open!

uses.rule: Changing trends use continuous.
uses.ex: Prices are rising every month.

traps.wrong: I am knowing him for years.
traps.right: I have known him for years.
traps.why: Know is stative, and 'for years' needs present perfect.
traps.bn: 'আমি তাকে বহু বছর ধরে চিনি' — বাংলায় present, ইংরেজিতে present perfect।

traps.wrong: He go to office every day.
traps.right: He goes to the office every day.
traps.bn: Third person singular-এ verb-এর সাথে s/es বসবে।

traps.wrong: Where you are going?
traps.right: Where are you going?
traps.why: In a question the helper verb comes before the subject.
traps.bn: প্রশ্নে auxiliary আগে, subject পরে।

drills.q: Your friend calls. You are in the middle of cooking.
drills.s: Can I call you back? I ___ dinner.
drills.x: The action is happening right now, so present continuous.

drills.q: Talking about your job in an interview.
drills.s: I ___ for a software company in Gulshan.
drills.x: A permanent job is a fact about you: present simple. 'I'm working' would suggest a temporary job.

drills.s: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
drills.x: Scientific facts use present simple; 'water' is singular so add -s.

drills.q: Your brother is usually lazy, but this week is different.
drills.s: He ___ really hard this week because exams start on Sunday.
drills.x: Temporary situation (this week): present continuous.

o: I am wanting a cup of tea.
I want a cup of tea.
I wanting a cup of tea.
I am want a cup of tea.
drills.a: I want a cup of tea.
drills.x: Want is a stative verb, so no -ing.

drills.q: Your colleague asks why you look worried.
drills.s: I ___ about whether to accept the offer from Dubai.
drills.x: Think = considering, an activity, so continuous is correct here.

drills.q: সে সবসময় দেরি করে আসে! (বিরক্তি নিয়ে)
drills.x: Always + continuous shows annoyance. 'He always comes late' is neutral.

drills.s: The sea level ___ every year.
drills.x: A changing trend: present continuous.

drills.q: You are looking at your friend's new car.
drills.s: This car ___ to my uncle, not to me.
drills.x: Belong is stative (possession). Never continuous.
Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb-ing.

drills.s: Hurry up! The train ___ at 7:40.
drills.x: Timetables use present simple, even for the future.

drills.s: Rahim gets the ball, ___ past two defenders and shoots!
drills.x: Live commentary of quick actions uses present simple.

drills.q: Telling a joke or story in a lively way.
drills.s: So yesterday this man ___ into my shop and asks for a refund.
drills.x: The 'historic present' makes a past story feel immediate, common in spoken English.

drills.q: Pick the correct sentence (look and taste are verbs of perception here).
o: This soup is tasting too salty.
This soup has tasting too salty.
drills.x: Taste = has a flavour, a state. 'I'm tasting the soup' (the action of trying it) is fine.

drills.q: Your friend is unusually rude today.
drills.s: He ___ very selfish today. That's not like him.
drills.x: Be + -ing describes temporary behaviour, not a permanent quality.

units.title: Present perfect vs past simple
units.idea: Past simple = finished time (yesterday, in 2019, ago). Present perfect = past action connected to now, time not stated or not finished.
units.ideaBn: সময় নির্দিষ্ট আর শেষ হলে past simple; সময় বলা নেই বা এখনো চলছে (today, this week, ever) হলে present perfect।

timeline.label: past simple: I lost my phone yesterday
present perfect: I've lost my phone (still lost)

uses.rule: Finished time word = past simple. Never 'I have seen him yesterday'.
uses.bn: yesterday, last, ago, in 2020, when থাকলে present perfect নয়।
uses.ex: I saw him yesterday.

uses.rule: Experience in life, no time given: present perfect.
uses.bn: জীবনে কখনো করেছ কিনা — present perfect।
uses.ex: Have you ever been to Cox's Bazar?

uses.rule: Result now: present perfect.
uses.ex: I've cut my finger. It's bleeding.

uses.rule: Unfinished period (today, this week, this year) = present perfect.
uses.ex: I've had three cups of tea today.

uses.rule: Just, already, yet go with present perfect in British English.
uses.ex: Has the parcel arrived yet? It's just arrived.

uses.rule: Once you add details (where, when, how), switch to past simple.
uses.bn: খবর জানানোর পর বিস্তারিত বললে past simple।
uses.ex: I've been to Nepal. I went there in 2022 and climbed a small peak.

traps.wrong: I have met him yesterday.
traps.right: I met him yesterday.
traps.bn: 'গতকাল দেখা করেছি' — বাংলায় 'করেছি' দেখে present perfect ভাববেন না।

traps.wrong: When have you arrived?
traps.right: When did you arrive?
traps.bn: When দিয়ে প্রশ্নে present perfect হয় না।

traps.wrong: I didn't finish yet.
traps.right: I haven't finished yet.
traps.bn: 'এখনো শেষ করিনি' = haven't finished yet।

drills.q: Your boss asks about the report. It is ready now.
drills.s: Yes, I ___ it. It's on your desk.
drills.x: Result now, no time given: present perfect.

drills.s: I ___ my wallet on the bus last night.
drills.x: 'Last night' is finished time: past simple.

o: I have never flown in a plane.
I never flew in a plane.
I didn't ever fly in a plane.
I am never flying in a plane.
drills.a: I have never flown in a plane.
drills.x: Life experience up to now: have never + V3.

o: I have seen that film in 2021.
I have saw that film in 2021.
I had see that film in 2021.
drills.x: In 2021 = finished time, so past simple.

drills.q: It's 3 pm. You keep drinking tea.
drills.s: I ___ four cups of tea today.
drills.x: Today is not finished: present perfect.

drills.s: When ___ in Dhaka?
drills.x: When asks for a point in finished time: past simple.

drills.q: Your sister shows you her new phone.
drills.s: Wow! How long ___ it?
drills.x: From the past up to now (and she still has it): present perfect.

drills.s: The prime minister ___ a new metro line. It opened this morning.
drills.x: New news, result now: present perfect. Details (this morning) would follow in past simple.

o: Did you finish your homework yet?
Have you finished your homework yet?
Have you finish your homework yet?
Are you finished your homework yet?
drills.a: Have you finished your homework yet?
drills.x: Yet → present perfect, with V3 'finished'.

drills.q: Your grandfather died in 2015. You talk about his life.
drills.s: He ___ in the army for twenty years.
drills.x: His life is finished, so the period is finished: past simple.

drills.q: Your friend still works at the bank.
drills.s: She ___ at that bank since 2018.
drills.x: Since + start point, still true now: present perfect.

drills.q: Your friend is still at the company and has achieved a lot.
drills.s: This is the third time she ___ promoted this year.
drills.x: 'This is the first/second/third time' takes present perfect.

o: It's the first time I eat sushi.
It's the first time I've eaten sushi.
It's the first time I ate sushi.
It's the first time I'm eating sushi.
drills.a: It's the first time I've eaten sushi.
drills.x: After 'It's the first time' use present perfect, never present simple.

drills.q: Your friend Arif is still alive and writing.
drills.s: Arif ___ five novels. (He may write more.)
drills.x: Living person, career not finished: present perfect. For a dead writer: wrote.

drills.q: আমি এই সপ্তাহে তাকে দেখিনি, যদিও গত সপ্তাহে দুবার দেখেছিলাম।
o: I haven't seen him this week, though I saw him twice last week.
I didn't see him this week, though I have seen him twice last week.
I haven't seen him this week, though I have seen him twice last week.
I don't see him this week, though I saw him twice last week.
drills.a: I haven't seen him this week, though I saw him twice last week.
drills.x: This week (unfinished) = present perfect; last week (finished) = past simple. Both in one sentence.

units.title: Present perfect continuous, since and for
units.idea: Have been + -ing = an activity from the past until now, focus on duration or on visible effects. Present perfect = focus on the result or the number.
units.ideaBn: কতক্ষণ ধরে করছি সেটা জোর দিলে have been + ing; কতগুলো/কী ফল হলো সেটা জোর দিলে have + V3।

timeline.label: I've been waiting for two hours

formula.name: Since / for
formula.pos: since + start point (2019, Monday, I was a child)

uses.rule: Duration until now: have been + -ing.
uses.ex: It has been raining since morning.

uses.rule: Visible effect of a recent activity.
uses.ex: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?

uses.rule: How many / how much = present perfect simple.
uses.ex: I've written three emails. (not: I've been writing three emails)

uses.rule: Stative verbs stay in simple form even with duration.
uses.bn: know, have (own), be — continuous হয় না।
uses.ex: I've known her since school.

uses.rule: Since takes a point in time; for takes a length of time.
uses.bn: since = কখন থেকে, for = কতদিন ধরে।
uses.ex: since 2010 / for fourteen years

traps.wrong: I am waiting here for two hours.
traps.right: I have been waiting here for two hours.
traps.why: From the past until now = perfect continuous.
traps.bn: 'আমি দুই ঘণ্টা ধরে অপেক্ষা করছি' — বাংলায় present continuous মনে হলেও ইংরেজিতে have been waiting।

traps.wrong: I live in Dhaka since 2015.
traps.right: I have lived / have been living in Dhaka since 2015.
traps.bn: since থাকলে সাধারণত present perfect বা perfect continuous।

traps.wrong: I have been reading since two hours.
traps.right: I have been reading for two hours.
traps.why: Two hours is a length: for.
traps.bn: সময়ের পরিমাণ হলে for।

drills.q: আমি সকাল থেকে তোমার জন্য অপেক্ষা করছি।
o: I have been waiting for you since morning.
I am waiting for you since morning.
I wait for you since morning.
I was waiting for you since morning.
drills.a: I have been waiting for you since morning.
drills.x: Started in the past, still going: have been + -ing, with since.

drills.s: Sorry, I ___ all the way from the bus stop.
drills.x: Visible effect (sweat) of a recent activity: perfect continuous.

drills.s: So far I ___ 40 pages of the report.
drills.x: A number of pages (result) = present perfect simple.

drills.s: She has been teaching at this school ___ 2012.
drills.x: 2012 is a starting point: since.

drills.s: We have been friends ___ more than a decade.
drills.x: More than a decade is a length: for.

o: I have been knowing her since school.
I have known her since school.
I am knowing her since school.
drills.a: I have known her since school.
drills.x: Know is stative, so perfect simple even with duration.

drills.s: It ___ . The streets are full of water.
drills.x: Visible result of a recent ongoing activity.

drills.s: How long ___ this headache?
drills.x: Both can appear, but 'have' (suffer from) is usually stative: 'How long have you had...' is the natural question.

o: He is working here for five years.
He has been working here for five years.
He works here since five years.
He has been working here since five years.
drills.a: He has been working here for five years.
drills.x: Duration until now + for + length.

drills.q: Your mother sees paint on your hands.
drills.s: What ___ ? There's paint all over your hands.
drills.x: Asking about a recent activity with visible signs: What have you been doing?

drills.q: A colleague looks tired and you want to know the activity, not the result.
drills.s: You look exhausted. ___ overtime again?
drills.x: Visible effect, focus on the activity: perfect continuous.

drills.s: The plumber ___ the pipe. You can use the tap now.
drills.x: Completed result: simple. 'Has been fixing' would mean the work may not be finished.

drills.s: It's ages since I ___ you!
drills.x: 'It's (time) since + past simple' marks the last time it happened.

o: I haven't been seeing her for months.
I haven't seen her for months.
I don't see her for months.
I'm not seeing her since months.
drills.a: I haven't seen her for months.
drills.x: Negative duration of a single action: present perfect simple. The continuous sounds wrong here.

units.title: Past simple, past continuous, used to, would
units.idea: Past continuous is the background scene; past simple is the event that happens in it. Used to and would describe old habits.
units.ideaBn: পেছনে চলতে থাকা কাজ past continuous; হঠাৎ ঘটে যাওয়া ঘটনা past simple।

uses.rule: Interrupted action: long action in continuous, short action in simple.
uses.ex: I was taking a shower when the power went out.

uses.rule: Two actions one after another: both past simple.
uses.ex: When he came in, I stood up. (first came, then stood)

uses.rule: Past continuous for a scene at a specific time.
uses.ex: At 10 pm last night I was watching the match.

uses.rule: Used to = past habit or state that is no longer true.
uses.ex: I used to live in Rajshahi.

uses.rule: Would = repeated past action only, not states.
uses.bn: would শুধু কাজের অভ্যাসে, অবস্থায় নয়।
uses.ex: Every Eid we would visit our grandparents. (but not: I would live in Rajshahi)

traps.wrong: When I reached, he was left.
traps.right: When I arrived, he had left.
traps.why: Earlier action = past perfect; 'reach' needs an object.
traps.bn: 'আমি পৌঁছানোর আগেই সে চলে গিয়েছিল' = had left।

traps.wrong: I use to play cricket when I was young.
traps.right: I used to play cricket when I was young.
traps.bn: positive-এ used to, negative/প্রশ্নে use to।

traps.wrong: While I walked, I was seeing an accident.
traps.right: While I was walking, I saw an accident.
traps.bn: while এর পরে চলমান কাজ।

drills.q: A sudden event during a long one.
drills.s: I ___ dinner when the guests arrived.
drills.x: Background action: past continuous.

drills.s: When the teacher entered, the students ___ up.
drills.x: First the teacher entered, then they stood: both past simple.

drills.q: ছোটবেলায় আমি প্রতিদিন নদীতে সাঁতার কাটতাম।
o: As a child, I used to swim in the river every day.
As a child, I was swimming in the river every day.
As a child, I have swum in the river every day.
As a child, I use to swim in the river every day.
drills.a: As a child, I used to swim in the river every day.
drills.x: Old habit that has stopped: used to.

o: I would have long hair when I was a student.
I used to have long hair when I was a student.
I was having long hair when I was a student.
I use to have long hair when I was a student.
drills.a: I used to have long hair when I was a student.
drills.x: Having hair is a state, so would cannot be used. Used to works for states.

drills.s: What ___ at 9 pm last Friday?
drills.x: Activity in progress at a specific past time: past continuous.

drills.q: Two actions at the same time.
drills.s: While I was reading, my brother ___ music.
drills.x: Two long actions in parallel: both continuous.

drills.s: ___ you use to live near here?
drills.x: Questions: Did + subject + use to.

drills.s: As I was crossing the road, a rickshaw ___ me.
drills.x: Short sudden event: past simple. Hit-hit-hit.

drills.s: In the evenings my grandmother ___ tell us stories.
drills.x: Repeated past action: would (or used to).

o: She didn't used to like coffee.
She didn't use to like coffee.
She not used to like coffee.
She wasn't use to like coffee.
drills.a: She didn't use to like coffee.
drills.x: After didn't, the base form: use to.

drills.s: I ___ if you could help me with this form.
drills.x: Past continuous here makes a request softer and more polite, not past time.

drills.s: We ___ go to Sylhet, but the trains were cancelled.
drills.x: Future in the past: was/were going to for a plan that did not happen.

drills.q: Planned in the past, it happened later.
drills.s: I knew he ___ late, because he always is.
drills.x: Future seen from the past: would.

o: I was used to walk to school every day.
I used to walk to school every day.
I am used to walk to school every day.
I would to walk to school every day.
drills.a: I used to walk to school every day.
drills.x: 'Be used to' means accustomed and takes -ing (I'm used to walking). 'Used to' + base is the old habit.

drills.q: আমি গরমে অভ্যস্ত, তাই আমার কোনো সমস্যা হয় না।
o: I'm used to the heat, so it doesn't bother me.
I used to the heat, so it doesn't bother me.
I use to heat, so it doesn't bother me.
I'm used to be hot, so it doesn't bother me.
drills.a: I'm used to the heat, so it doesn't bother me.
drills.x: Be used to + noun / -ing = accustomed to.

units.title: Past perfect and past perfect continuous
units.idea: Past perfect = the earlier of two past actions, the 'past of the past'. Use it only when the order matters.
units.ideaBn: অতীতের দুটি কাজের মধ্যে যেটি আগে ঘটেছিল তাতে had + V3।

formula.name: Past perfect continuous
formula.q: How long had you been waiting?

uses.rule: The earlier action when you look back from a past moment.
uses.bn: পরের ঘটনার আগেই যা হয়ে গিয়েছিল।
uses.ex: By the time we got to the station, the train had left.

uses.rule: Experience up to a past point.
uses.ex: It was the first time I had seen snow.

uses.rule: Duration up to a past point: had been + -ing.
uses.bn: অতীতের এক সময় পর্যন্ত কতক্ষণ চলছিল।
uses.ex: She was tired because she had been working all night.

uses.rule: After 'before' or 'after' the order is clear, so past simple is also fine.
uses.ex: I left after he arrived. = I left after he had arrived.

uses.rule: Do not use past perfect just because something is 'long ago'.
uses.bn: অনেক আগের ঘটনা মানেই past perfect নয়।
uses.ex: My father was born in 1960. (not: had been born)

traps.wrong: I had gone to Cox's Bazar last year.
traps.right: I went to Cox's Bazar last year.
traps.why: Only one past action; no earlier past.
traps.bn: শুধু 'অনেক আগে' বলে had ব্যবহার করবেন না। অন্য একটি অতীত ঘটনার আগে হলে তবেই।

traps.wrong: When I reached the class, the teacher already started.
traps.right: When I reached the class, the teacher had already started.
traps.why: The start came before my arrival.
traps.bn: আগেই শুরু হয়ে গিয়েছিল = had already started।

traps.wrong: He told me he has finished.
traps.right: He told me he had finished.
traps.bn: told দিয়ে বললে has → had।

drills.q: You arrive late at the cinema.
drills.s: When we got there, the film ___ .
drills.x: The film started before we got there: had + V3.

drills.q: আমি পৌঁছানোর আগেই সভা শেষ হয়ে গিয়েছিল।
o: The meeting had ended before I arrived.
The meeting has ended before I arrived.
The meeting was ending before I arrived.
The meeting ended before I had been arriving.
drills.a: The meeting had ended before I arrived.
drills.x: Earlier past action: had ended.

drills.s: It was the first time I ___ on a plane.
drills.x: Experience up to that past moment: past perfect.

drills.s: She was exhausted because she ___ for twelve hours.
drills.x: Duration up to a past point: had been + -ing.

o: My grandfather had been born in 1940.
My grandfather has been born in 1940.
drills.x: A single past fact: past simple. 'Long ago' alone is no reason for past perfect.

drills.s: He couldn't pay because he ___ his wallet at home.
drills.x: Leaving the wallet happened before not paying.

drills.q: Ground was wet in the morning.
drills.s: The ground was wet. It ___ all night.
drills.x: Activity lasting until a past moment, with a visible result then.

drills.s: After I ___ my homework, I went to play.
drills.x: With 'after', both past perfect and past simple are correct.

drills.s: She ___ in front of so many people before.
drills.x: Experience up to that past day: had never + V3.

drills.q: Narrative, emphasis on what was hardly finished.
drills.s: Hardly ___ home when the phone rang.
drills.x: Hardly / No sooner + inverted past perfect: Hardly had I got home when...

drills.s: No sooner ___ than the storm began.
drills.x: No sooner + had + subject + V3 + than.

drills.s: I ___ to finish by noon, but the internet went down.
drills.x: Past perfect of hope/intend/expect for a plan that failed.

o: When I had arrived, I took a taxi.
When I arrived, I had taken a taxi.
After I had checked in, I went to my room.
After I had check in, I went to my room.
drills.a: After I had checked in, I went to my room.
drills.x: Past perfect for the earlier action; V3 is 'checked'.

units.title: Future: will, going to, present continuous, present simple
units.idea: Will = decision now, promise, prediction from opinion. Going to = plan already made, prediction from evidence. Present continuous = fixed arrangement. Present simple = timetable.
units.ideaBn: এখনই সিদ্ধান্ত নিলে will; আগে থেকে পরিকল্পনা থাকলে going to; সময়-তারিখ ঠিক করা থাকলে present continuous।

timeline.label: plan made before → I'm going to

uses.rule: Decision at the moment of speaking: will.
uses.ex: The phone's ringing. I'll get it.

uses.rule: Plan or intention made earlier: going to.
uses.ex: I'm going to apply for a master's in Canada.

uses.rule: Evidence you can see now: going to.
uses.ex: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.

uses.rule: Arrangement with time and people fixed: present continuous.
uses.ex: I'm meeting the client at 3 tomorrow.

uses.rule: Offers, promises, threats, refusals: will / won't.
uses.ex: I won't tell anyone, I promise.

uses.rule: Shall I / shall we for offers and suggestions.
uses.ex: Shall I open the window?

traps.wrong: I will go to my cousin's wedding next Friday. I booked the bus.
traps.right: I'm going to my cousin's wedding next Friday.
traps.why: Fixed arrangement: present continuous (or going to).
traps.bn: সব ঠিকঠাক থাকলে will নয়, present continuous ভালো।

traps.wrong: Wait, I am going to help you!
traps.right: Wait, I'll help you!
traps.bn: এই মুহূর্তের সিদ্ধান্ত = will।

traps.wrong: Will I open the door?
traps.right: Shall I open the door?
traps.bn: প্রস্তাব দিতে Shall I।

drills.q: Your friend says, 'I have no pen.' You decide now.
drills.s: No problem, I ___ you mine.
drills.x: Decision made at the moment of speaking: will.

drills.q: You decided last month to learn driving.
drills.s: I ___ learn to drive this winter.
drills.x: Plan made before: going to.

drills.s: Take an umbrella. It ___ rain.
drills.x: Prediction from present evidence: going to.

drills.q: আমি কাল সকাল দশটায় ডাক্তারের সাথে দেখা করছি। (অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট নেওয়া আছে)
o: I'm seeing the doctor at 10 tomorrow morning.
I see the doctor at 10 tomorrow morning.
I would see the doctor at 10 tomorrow morning.
I have seen the doctor at 10 tomorrow morning.
drills.a: I'm seeing the doctor at 10 tomorrow morning.
drills.x: Arrangement with a time: present continuous.

drills.s: Our flight to Chattogram ___ at 6:15 tomorrow.
drills.x: Official timetables: present simple.
Offer with I: Shall I...?

drills.s: Don't worry, I ___ late again.
drills.x: Promises use will / won't.

drills.s: I think Bangladesh ___ the match tomorrow.
drills.x: Prediction based on opinion (I think): will.

drills.s: The car ___ start! I've tried five times.
drills.x: Won't for a refusal, even for machines.

drills.q: You're about to leave right this second.
drills.s: Hurry, the train ___ leave!
drills.x: Be about to = very near future.

drills.s: The President ___ visit Rajshahi next month.
drills.x: Be to + base = formal arrangement, common in news.

drills.q: Asking for a decision or advice.
drills.s: What ___ we do now? The shop is closed.
drills.x: Shall we...? asks for a suggestion or decision.

drills.q: আমি আগামীকাল এই সময়ে পরীক্ষা দিচ্ছি থাকব।
o: I'll be taking an exam at this time tomorrow.
I take an exam at this time tomorrow.
I'll have taken an exam at this time tomorrow.
I'm going to take an exam at this time tomorrow ago.
drills.a: I'll be taking an exam at this time tomorrow.
drills.x: In progress at a future point: future continuous.

units.title: Future continuous and future perfect
units.idea: Future continuous = in progress at a future moment. Future perfect = finished before a future moment (by + time).
units.ideaBn: ভবিষ্যতের এক সময়ে চলতে থাকবে → will be + ing; সেই সময়ের মধ্যেই শেষ হয়ে যাবে → will have + V3।

formula.name: Future continuous
formula.q: Will you be using the car tonight?

formula.name: Future perfect
formula.q: Will you have finished by Friday?

uses.rule: Action in progress at a future time.
uses.ex: This time next week I'll be lying on the beach.

uses.rule: Polite question about plans (not a request).
uses.ex: Will you be using the printer this afternoon?

uses.rule: Finished before a future deadline: by + time.
uses.ex: By December, we'll have built the second floor.

uses.rule: Duration up to a future point: will have been + -ing.
uses.ex: In June I'll have been working here for ten years.

traps.wrong: By next year I will finish my degree.
traps.right: By next year I will have finished my degree.
traps.why: By + time = finished before then: future perfect.
traps.bn: by থাকলে will have + V3 বেশি স্বাভাবিক।

traps.wrong: Don't call at 9, I will sleep.
traps.right: Don't call at 9, I will be sleeping.
traps.bn: সেই সময়ে ঘুমাতে থাকব = will be sleeping।

drills.s: At 9 I ___ my exam, so my phone will be off.
drills.x: In progress at a future moment: will be + -ing.

drills.s: By Friday, the team ___ the app.
drills.x: Completed before the deadline: future perfect.

drills.q: আগামী মাসের মধ্যে আমি বইটি শেষ করে ফেলব।
o: I will have finished the book by next month.
I finish the book by next month.
I am finishing the book by next month.
I had finished the book by next month.
drills.a: I will have finished the book by next month.
drills.x: By + future time: will have + V3.

drills.s: ___ the car tonight? I need it.
drills.x: Future continuous makes a soft, polite question about plans.

drills.s: Next March, my father ___ at the bank for 30 years.
drills.x: Duration up to a future point: will have been + -ing (or will have worked).

o: By the time you arrive, we will eat.
By the time you arrive, we will have eaten.
By the time you will arrive, we will have eaten.
By the time you arrive, we have ate.
drills.a: By the time you arrive, we will have eaten.
drills.x: After 'by the time' use present simple (you arrive); main clause future perfect.

drills.s: This time tomorrow we ___ over the Himalayas.
drills.x: In progress at that moment.

drills.s: By 2030, scientists ___ a cure, I hope.
drills.x: Completed before a future point: future perfect.

drills.s: Don't call Mina now. She ___ dinner at this time.
drills.x: Will be + -ing can also guess what is happening now.

drills.s: It's 6 pm. The parcel ___ by now.
drills.x: Will have + V3 = confident guess that something has already happened.

units.title: Time clauses and conditionals
units.idea: After when, if, as soon as, until, before, after, unless: no will. Use present for the future. Conditionals shift tense to show how real or unreal something is.
units.ideaBn: when/if/as soon as/until এর পরে ভবিষ্যৎ বোঝাতেও will বসে না, present বসে। অবাস্তব কল্পনায় tense এক ধাপ পিছিয়ে যায়।

formula.name: First (real future)
formula.neg: If it rains, we'll stay in.

formula.name: Second (unreal now)
formula.neg: If I had money, I'd buy it.

formula.name: Third (unreal past)
formula.pos: If + had V3, would have + V3
formula.neg: If I had known, I'd have come.

formula.name: Mixed
formula.neg: If I had studied, I'd be a doctor now.

uses.rule: No will after time words for the future.
uses.ex: I'll call you when I get home. (not: when I will get home)

uses.rule: Present perfect in the time clause to stress completion.
uses.bn: আগে শেষ হওয়াটা জোর দিতে have + V3।
uses.ex: You can go out after you've finished your homework.

uses.rule: Second conditional for imaginary present; use were for all subjects in formal English.
uses.ex: If I were you, I'd take the job.

uses.rule: Third conditional for regrets about the past.
uses.ex: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.

uses.rule: Wish + past = unreal now; wish + had V3 = regret about the past.
uses.bn: wish এর পরেও tense পিছিয়ে যায়।
uses.ex: I wish I lived closer. I wish I hadn't said that.

traps.wrong: I will call you when I will reach.
traps.right: I'll call you when I reach / get there.
traps.bn: 'পৌঁছে ফোন দেব' — when এর পরে present।

traps.wrong: If I would have money, I would buy a flat.
traps.right: If I had money, I would buy a flat.
traps.bn: if অংশে would বসে না।

traps.wrong: If I knew, I would have told you.
traps.right: If I had known, I would have told you.
traps.bn: অতীতের অবাস্তব শর্তে had known।

drills.s: I'll text you as soon as I ___ in Chattogram.
drills.x: After 'as soon as', present simple for the future.

drills.q: আমি যদি তুমি হতাম, চাকরিটা নিতাম।
o: If I were you, I would take the job.
If I am you, I will take the job.
If I would be you, I would take the job.
If I had been you, I take the job.
drills.a: If I were you, I would take the job.
drills.x: Imaginary present: If + were, would + base.

drills.q: You missed the bus because you woke up late.
drills.s: If I ___ up earlier, I wouldn't have missed the bus.
drills.x: Unreal past: If + had + V3.

o: Unless you will hurry, you'll be late.
Unless you hurry, you'll be late.
Unless you don't hurry, you'll be late.
Unless you hurried, you'll be late.
drills.a: Unless you hurry, you'll be late.
drills.x: Unless = if not. No will and no extra 'not'.

drills.s: I wish I ___ a better salary.
drills.x: Wish about the present: past simple.

drills.s: If I had taken that job in Singapore, I ___ there now.
drills.x: Past condition, present result: would + base (or would be + -ing).

drills.s: I wish I ___ that to her. She was so upset.
drills.x: Regret about the past: wish + had + V3.

drills.s: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
drills.x: First conditional: If + present, will + base.

o: Wait here until I will come back.
Wait here until I come back.
Wait here until I am coming back.
Wait here until I came back.
drills.a: Wait here until I come back.
drills.x: After until: present simple.

drills.s: You can leave once you ___ the form.
drills.x: Present perfect after 'once' stresses that signing must be completed first.

drills.s: ___ you need any help, please call the front desk.
drills.x: Inverted 'Should you...' = If you should... (formal).

drills.s: ___ I known about the strike, I would have stayed home.
drills.x: Inversion: Had I known = If I had known.

drills.s: It's high time you ___ a proper job.
drills.x: It's (high) time + past simple, but the meaning is present.

drills.s: I'd rather you ___ smoke in the car.
drills.x: Would rather + another subject + past simple.

drills.s: He talks as if he ___ the boss, but he isn't.
drills.x: As if + past for something not true.

drills.q: Regret: a modal in the past.
drills.s: You ___ me. I would have helped you.
drills.x: Should have + V3 = criticism or regret about the past.

drills.s: The road is wet. It ___ in the night.
drills.x: Must have + V3 = strong certainty about the past.

o: If I would have known, I would have come.
If I had known, I would have came.
If I had known, I would have come.
If I knew, I will have come.
drills.a: If I had known, I would have come.
drills.x: Third conditional: had + V3, would have + V3 (come).

drills.q: সে হয়তো বাসটা মিস করেছে, তাই দেরি হচ্ছে।
o: He might have missed the bus, so he's late.
He might miss the bus, so he's late.
He must miss the bus, so he's late.
He might has missed the bus, so he's late.
drills.a: He might have missed the bus, so he's late.
drills.x: Might have + V3 = a possibility about the past.

units.title: Reported speech and tense agreement
units.idea: When the reporting verb is past (said, told, asked), move the tense one step back, unless the fact is still true and you want to show that.
units.ideaBn: said/told দিয়ে অন্যের কথা বললে tense এক ধাপ পেছায়: is → was, has done → had done, will → would।

timeline.label: now: She said she was tired.

formula.name: Backshift
formula.q: is going to → was going to

formula.name: Questions
formula.q: She asked if/whether I was free.

uses.rule: Move one step back after a past reporting verb.
uses.ex: 'I'm busy.' → He said he was busy.

uses.rule: Still true facts can keep the original tense.
uses.bn: চিরসত্য বা এখনো সত্য হলে না বদলালেও চলে।
uses.ex: She said Dhaka is the capital. / He said he lives in Mirpur (he still does).

uses.rule: Reported questions use statement word order, no do/does/did.
uses.ex: He asked me where I worked.

uses.rule: Commands: tell/ask + object + to + base.
uses.ex: She told me to wait outside. She asked me not to shout.

uses.rule: Present reporting verb (says) = no change.
uses.ex: He says he is coming.

traps.wrong: He told that he is sick.
traps.right: He said that he was sick. / He told me that he was sick.
traps.why: Tell needs a person; backshift after past.
traps.bn: told এর পরে কাকে বলেছে সেটা লাগে।

traps.wrong: She asked me where do I live.
traps.right: She asked me where I lived.
traps.why: Statement word order in reported questions.
traps.bn: রিপোর্ট করা প্রশ্নে do/does বসে না।

traps.wrong: He said me to come.
traps.right: He told me to come.
traps.why: Say does not take a person directly.
traps.bn: said me নয়, told me।

drills.q: Report it. Rahim: 'I am working late.'
drills.s: Rahim said he ___ late.
drills.x: Present continuous → past continuous.

drills.q: Report it. Nadia: 'I have lost my keys.'
drills.s: Nadia said she ___ her keys.
drills.x: Present perfect → past perfect.

drills.q: Report it. Boss: 'I will call you tomorrow.'
drills.s: My boss said he ___ me the next day.
drills.x: Will → would; tomorrow → the next day.

o: She asked me where did I work.
She asked me where I worked.
She asked me where was I working.
She asked to me where I work.
drills.a: She asked me where I worked.
drills.x: Statement word order and backshift.

drills.q: সে আমাকে বাইরে অপেক্ষা করতে বলল।
o: He told me to wait outside.
He said me to wait outside.
He said to me that wait outside.
drills.a: He told me to wait outside.
drills.x: Command: tell + person + to + base.

drills.q: Report a yes/no question. 'Are you free on Friday?'
drills.s: He asked me ___ free on Friday.
drills.x: Yes/no questions: if / whether + statement order + backshift.

drills.s: Our teacher told us that the earth ___ around the sun.
drills.x: A permanent truth can stay in the present.

drills.s: She said she ___ come.
drills.x: Can → could.

drills.s: The electrician warned us ___ the wires.
drills.x: Warn/tell + object + not to + base.

drills.s: She suggested ___ a taxi.
drills.x: Suggest + -ing (or suggest that we take). Never 'suggested us to'.

drills.s: He said he ___ the day before.
drills.x: Past continuous → past perfect continuous; yesterday → the day before.

o: He asked me what time is it.
He asked me what time it was.
He asked me what time was it.
He asked to me what time it is.
drills.a: He asked me what time it was.
drills.x: Statement order and backshift in reported questions.

mastery.s: I ___ in marketing for six years, and I currently manage a team of five.
mastery.x: From the past until now with 'for': perfect continuous.

mastery.s: I ___ the invoice yesterday, but I'll send it again.
mastery.x: Yesterday: past simple.

mastery.q: আমি যখন ফোন করলাম, সে তখন রান্না করছিল।
o: When I called, she was cooking.
When I was calling, she cooked.
When I have called, she was cooking.
mastery.a: When I called, she was cooking.
mastery.x: Short event (called) interrupts a background action (was cooking).

mastery.s: I can't talk now. I ___ the car.
mastery.x: Right now: present continuous.

o: I have been living here since 2019.
mastery.a: I have been living here since 2019.
mastery.x: Since + still true: perfect (continuous).

mastery.s: By the time I got there, most people ___ .
mastery.x: Earlier past: past perfect.

mastery.s: Don't worry. I ___ the slides by the meeting.
mastery.x: By + future point: future perfect.

o: Have you ever been to the Sundarbans?
Did you ever go to the Sundarbans?
Were you ever gone to the Sundarbans?
Do you ever go to the Sundarbans?
mastery.a: Have you ever been to the Sundarbans?
mastery.x: Life experience: Have you ever been...? (British). 'Did you ever go' is American and less common in exams.

mastery.s: We ___ a new flat next month. We've already signed the contract.
mastery.x: Fixed arrangement: present continuous.

mastery.s: I'll lend you the book after I ___ it.
mastery.x: No will after 'after'. Present perfect stresses that reading is finished first.

o: If I had known about the traffic, I would leave earlier.
If I had known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
If I knew about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
If I would know about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
mastery.a: If I had known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
mastery.x: Third conditional: had + V3, would have + V3.

mastery.s: The manager told us the shop ___ at 10 the next day.
mastery.x: Will → would after a past reporting verb.

mastery.s: He ___ his music at midnight. I can't sleep!
mastery.x: Always + continuous: annoyance.

mastery.s: When we were kids, we ___ cricket on the roof every evening.
mastery.x: Past habit: used to / would / past simple.
You can see it about to happen: going to.

mastery.q: আমি তিনটা ইমেইল লিখেছি, আরো দুটো বাকি।
o: I've written three emails, and two more are left.
I've been writing three emails, and two more are left.
I wrote three emails, and two more are left yesterday.
I'm writing three emails, and two more left.
mastery.a: I've written three emails, and two more are left.
mastery.x: A number (three) = present perfect simple.

mastery.s: I wish it ___ so hot today.
mastery.x: Wish + past for the present. 'Weren't' is the formal form for all subjects.
Think = opinion, a state: present simple.

mastery.s: She was crying because she ___ bad news from home.
mastery.x: The news came before the crying: past perfect.

o: When did you have seen him?
mastery.x: When + past simple question.

decide.q: Does the sentence have a finished time (yesterday, ago, in 2020, last)?
Did it start in the past and is it still true or still going (since, for, so far, today)?
decide.yes: Present perfect (simple for results and numbers, continuous for duration).

decide.q: Is it about the past, but before another past event?
Is it a background action when something else happened?
Is it a fact, habit, or timetable?
Is it happening now, temporary, or a changing trend?
Is it future after when / if / until / as soon as?
decide.yes: Present simple (or present perfect), no will.

decide.q: Is it future: decided now, planned, or arranged?
decide.yes: Now: will. Planned: going to. Arranged with a time: present continuous.

decide.q: Will it be finished before a future deadline (by)?
